narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the total amount you wanted to borrow. The requested duration of 48 months was the most important reason for the rejection. At more than twice the average length of approved loans (19 months), this long repayment period strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Your checking account status came second. Having a negative balance puts you in a relatively small group (only 13% of applicants), and this situation also increased the likelihood of being seen as high risk. The loan amount of 4,308 DM was the third most influential factor. Although a larger amount slightly worked in your favor compared with the average of approved loans (3,020 DM), its positive effect was not strong enough to overcome the concerns created by the long duration and account status.

Taken together, these three features led the model to conclude that the risk was too high to approve the loan. To improve your chances in the future, consider applying for a shorter loan term with a smaller amount and, if possible, resolve the negative balance in your checking account before reapplying.
